description: How one client text frame's payload is read as a protocol v0 message (docs/protocol.md, "Client → server"): the bytes are read as Foundation's JSONSerialization reads them, the root must be an object whose "type" is a string, else malformed. hello needs a non-empty string token (not trimmed), and its protocol field, read through NSNumber.intValue when it is a JSON number and otherwise ignored, must be 0 (missing means 0); the token is checked first. intent maps its "intent" name ("" when absent or not a string) and, for sendPrompt, its string "text" through the protocol name table (intent-names.json); a name the table refuses is unknown_intent. ping takes no fields. Any other type is unknown_type. Unknown fields are always ignored. A failure is answered with an error message whose code and message are contract (HK-229); what the listener then does (close 1002 for malformed, bad_hello and unsupported_protocol, keep the connection otherwise) is the connection policy's.
function: protocol::message::parse_client_message (Swift: CoreBridge.clientMessage(_:); until slice 2.6 PowerUpProtocol.parseClientMessage(_:)) — input the frame payload (a bytes descriptor), expected the message ({"type": "hello", "token"}, {"type": "intent", <intent descriptor fields>}, {"type": "ping"}) or the error it is answered with ({"error": <code>, "message": <text>})
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.7, v2.15; docs/protocol.md spec v0; Tests/PowerUpTests/ProtocolFixtureTests.swift testClientMessageTable plays it through the bridge (CoreBridge.clientMessage(_:)). Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/protocol.rs client_message_cases runs protocol::message::parse_client_message.
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 Foundation and CryptoKit (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 2d20afb

cases.name: protocol 2^32 is unsupported

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 4294967296.

cases.reason: The version is a 64-bit integer: 2^32 is not 0.

cases.name: protocol Int64 max is unsupported

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 9223372036854775807.

cases.reason: The largest Int64 is named as sent.

cases.name: protocol 2^63 wraps to the smallest Int64

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for -9223372036854775808.

cases.reason: One past Int64 is read unsigned, and NSNumber.intValue wraps it around: the message names -9223372036854775808.

cases.name: protocol 2^64 wraps to 0
cases.reason: Past UInt64 the literal is an NSDecimalNumber, whose intValue is the literal wrapped to 64 bits: 2^64 is 0, so the hello is accepted as version 0.

cases.name: protocol 2^64 + 1 wraps to 1

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 1.

cases.reason: The NSDecimalNumber's intValue wraps to 64 bits, so one past 2^64 asks for version 1.

cases.name: protocol 99999999999999999999 wraps

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 7766279631452241919.

cases.reason: Twenty nines wrapped to 64 bits.

cases.name: protocol one below Int64 min wraps to Int64 max

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 9223372036854775807.

cases.reason: A negative NSDecimalNumber wraps too: -2^63 - 1 reads as the largest Int64.

cases.name: protocol 2^128 keeps the digits a 128-bit mantissa holds

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for -6.

cases.reason: The mantissa is 128 bits: the last digit that would overflow it is dropped and raises the exponent, so the value is 2^128 - 6 and wraps to -6.

cases.name: protocol 9223372036854775808.0 wraps to the smallest Int64

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for -9223372036854775808.

cases.reason: More than 17 significant digits with a fraction is an NSDecimalNumber, not a double: 2^63 wraps to Int64.min instead of saturating.

cases.name: protocol 123456789012345678.5 is truncated exactly

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 123456789012345678.

cases.reason: An NSDecimalNumber keeps every digit (a double would read 123456789012345680).

cases.name: protocol 922337203685477582.3 divides the wrapped mantissa

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for -922337203685477579.

cases.reason: With a negative exponent intValue takes the mantissa's low 64 bits as a signed integer (9223372036854775823 is -9223372036854775793) and divides it toward zero.

cases.name: protocol 1.00000000000000000e20 counts its trailing zeros

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 7766279631452241920.

cases.reason: Eighteen digits, trailing zeros included, make an NSDecimalNumber: 10^20 wraps to 64 bits instead of saturating.

cases.name: protocol 0.92233720368547758e19 is a double

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 9223372036854775807.

cases.reason: The integer part's leading zero is not counted: 17 significant digits are a double, which saturates.

cases.name: protocol -0.00000000000000000001e40 counts the fraction's zeros

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for -7766279631452241920.

cases.reason: The fraction's leading zeros are counted: twenty digits make an NSDecimalNumber, -10^20 wrapped to 64 bits.

cases.name: protocol 1e30 saturates at the largest Int64

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for 9223372036854775807.

cases.reason: NSNumber.intValue of a double past Int64 saturates: the message names 9223372036854775807.

cases.name: protocol -1e30 saturates at the smallest Int64

expected.message: This server speaks protocol 0; you asked for -9223372036854775808.

cases.reason: NSNumber.intValue of a double below Int64 saturates: the message names -9223372036854775808.
